Drive Medical Deluxe Folding Bath Bench Review 2026

# Drive Medical Deluxe Folding Bath Bench Review 2026

 By The Chair Institute Updated on August 15, 2024 

## In a Nutshell:

A simple, sturdy, no-frills folding design. The Drive Medical Deluxe Folding Bath Bench is recommended for anyone with a slight to moderate mobility issue weighing up to 300 pounds, especially those who don’t have much space to work with.

### Overall Rating

##### 4.3/5

* Brand Reliability is a measure of the strength and longevity of the brand, which by extension, is a measure of the level of support you can expect.

### Benefits

- Modestly priced
- Comes with many features
- Well-made and reliable
- Collapses into a compact size
- Supports many weight and size

### Drawbacks

- Modest weight limit
- Not aesthetically pleasing

Recommended For: Anyone with a slight to moderate mobility issue weighing up to 300 pounds, especially those who don’t have much space to work with.

Have you reached a point where you’re having trouble moving around? Has your mobility issue made bathing a challenge? Are you a bit short on space? You will like what you read in this review if you answered yes to any of those questions.

Drive Medical is one of the most respected names in the industry. They make various medical devices, including shower chairs in various shapes and sizes. The Drive Medical Deluxe Folding Bath Bench is a lesson in simplicity and is about as basic as it gets. It does have its share of limitations, and as such, it might not be for everyone.

In the following sections, we’ll explain everything this stool offers so you can decide if this is the model you’ve been searching for. Let’s jump right in and take a closer look!

## Key Features of the Drive Medical Deluxe Folding Shower Chair

The Drive Medical Deluxe folding bath bench won’t win any beauty contests. That’s the first thing you’ll likely think of when you see the stool for the first time.

If aesthetics are important, falling in love with this little stool will be hard. While it’s true that it falls short of being outright ugly, it certainly won’t win any beauty contests either.

The good news is that while the design team responsible for this model didn’t put any effort into making their shower stool attractive, they did make it delightfully functional. You’ll find much to like here if that’s what you’re after. 

### Chair Specifications

Before we get into those details, let’s look at the core stats defining the model. Here are the key points:

- Chair Dimensions: 17.5 – 18.5” (H) x 20” (W) x 20.5” (D)
- Folded Dimensions: 27” x 22” x 4”
- Chair Weight: 4.5 pounds
- Maximum Supported Weight: 300 pounds
- Seat Height: 17.5” to 18.5”
- Seat Width: 20”
- Seat Depth: 12”

There’s a lot to like about these numbers, but only two potential snags exist. First, it’s an average-sized stool, which is good because it will work well with most showers and larger tubs. If you have a standard-sized tub or a pocket shower, though, this one won’t fit. You’ll need to look for something slightly smaller.

The seat height is adjustable, with the lowest setting just under the big and tall range and the highest setting just above it. That makes it useful for all but the shortest potential buyers, which is fantastic.

The seat width is a good fit for most of the market, but the depth is a bit underwhelming, and we’d rate it as the weakest point in the design. Even so, 12” is sufficient, given the time you will likely spend on the stool.

Most of the furniture on the market today supports 300 pounds of user weight, and the Drive Medical deluxe folding shower chair is no exception. As such, this stool is useful for 95% of the market. Take the manufacturer’s weight limit seriously, though. The last thing you want is to have it collapse under you while you’re in the shower, and plenty of models are available that will support more weight!

Finally, we love that this stool collapses to a tiny footprint, making it easy to store when it’s not in use. If you’ve got the space for it, fantastic! Just leave it in the shower all the time. If space is at a premium in your house, you’ll appreciate how easy it is to fold and store, a fact made even easier thanks to its delightfully lightweight!

### Adjustability and Comfort

There’s only one adjustable feature on offer here, and we already mentioned it. The length of the legs is easily adjustable, changing the seat’s height between 17.5” and 18.5”.

Comfort-wise, it’s about what you’d expect from a stool made of tubed aluminum and hard plastic, which is not great. Then again, given the time you’re likely to spend in it, it’s fine for most folks.

One thing to note is that the seat has several drainage holes, so you won’t find yourself sitting in puddles of water when using it. 

It’s a small detail but a very nice touch and exactly what you’d expect from one of the biggest and best-known companies in the industry.

While most shower stools offer fewer safety features than bench-style transfer seats or shower chairs, Drive Medical took pains to include as many safety features as possible. This includes the wide spacing of the legs and the rubberized feet, which give the stool a sure grip and make it very unlikely that it will slide away from you when you’re getting onto or off of it.

It’s a good addition, but be aware that if you have a serious mobility issue, you’ll probably need a more robust solution than a simple shower stool, preferably with no-slip handgrips. Note that this stool does offer handgrips, but they don’t feature a rubberized surface. So, the more serious your mobility condition is, the less confident you may feel about relying on them.

### No Assembly is Required

Another small but nice perk offered by the Drive Medical folding bath bench is that you don’t need to do anything before you can start using it. Just take it out of the box when it arrives, unfold it, and it’s ready to go! Given that most of the furniture you can buy online today has to be assembled, we were happy to see an exception to that rule.

## Drive Medical Deluxe Folding Bath Bench Pros and Cons

In no particular order, here are the things we think you’ll like best about this model:

- It’s very modestly priced 
- It comes with as many, if not more, safety features as you’d expect to see on a simple stool. 
- It is well made and with proper care, and it will provide years of reliable, hassle-free service. 
- It collapses into a nice, compact footprint, which makes storage between uses a simple matter. 
- It’s big enough and supports enough weight to make it a good fit for more than 90% of the market. 

On the flip side, if you weigh more than 300 pounds or are looking for something that will make a good accent piece and provide you with a convenient bathing platform, this model probably isn’t the one you’re after.

## Drive Medical Deluxe Folding Bath Bench Review Conclusion

We like the Drive Medical deluxe folding bath bench very much. Most people with mobility issues are more interested in safety features than they are worried about aesthetics. This one delivers style for a very modest price tag. If you weigh 300 pounds or less, we highly recommend it.

We evaluated the NOVA Shower and Bath Chair with Arms, which is exceptionally designed for serious mobility issues.

References & Resources

- Drive Medical, Official Brand Website.
- Drive Medical Folding Shower Chair Specifications Sheet.
- Why Shower Seats Are So Important, MED Ability.

Best Folding Shower Seats UK 2026: 7 Checked Against Manuals

# Best Foldable Shower Chairs and Seats UK: 7 Models Checked Against Their Makers’ Documents

Last Updated on November 12, 2026 | Published: October 17, 2024

 

Published 17 October 2024 · Last updated 12 November 2026

We compared seven foldable shower seats sold in the UK, six that fix to the shower wall and one freestanding folding stool, using their makers' own documents read on 18 September 2026. We did not test any of them. The Aidapt Solo Deluxe Shower Seat (VB535) is the best overall, with a back, flip-up arms and a 190kg limit in every Aidapt document. The Aidapt Solo Standard (VB532) is the best seat-only choice, with a 25 year frame warranty, and the NRS M48787 is the slimmest when folded, at 95mm. Three of the seven have maker documents that disagree with each other. A wall seat's printed limit assumes a sound wall and suitable fixings chosen by a competent installer.

- Seven foldable shower seats checked against their makers' documents on 18 September 2026. None were bought, used or measured.
- Best overall: Aidapt Solo Deluxe (VB535), a wall seat with a back, flip-up arms and a 190kg limit in every Aidapt document.
- Best seat-only choice: Aidapt Solo Standard (VB532), 190kg limit and a 25 year frame warranty.
- Best for a tight cubicle: NRS Folding Shower Seat with Legs (M48787), which projects 95mm from the wall when folded. Its limit is 160kg.
- The NRS seat with back and arms (M53370) is listed at 190kg on its product page but 160kg in its instructions.
- No drilling needed: Aidapt Aluminium Folding Shower Stool (VB541A), freestanding, with a 120kg limit.
- The printed user limit is the seat's limit, not the wall's. Fixings are left to the installer.
- Shower seats are often supplied free after an occupational therapy assessment through the council.

A folding shower seat lets you sit down to wash. Most fix to the shower wall and fold up out of the way. We looked at seven seats. We did not test them. We read what each maker says in its own documents. The Aidapt Solo Deluxe came first. It has a back and arms and takes 190kg. One seat here needs no drilling. It is a folding stool that stands on the floor, and it takes 120kg. A wall seat is only as strong as the wall it is fixed to. Ask a competent fitter to choose the right fixings. The seat should be about as high as the back of your knee. Ask your council first. It may supply and fit a seat free.

Last checked: 18 September 2026. Every specification on this page was read from the manufacturer’s own product page, leaflet, spec sheet or instructions on that date. We have not used these products; see how we checked. Links to Amazon are paid links, so we may earn a commission if you buy.

This page compares seven foldable shower seats sold in the UK: six fold-up seats that fix to the shower wall and one freestanding folding stool. We have not tested any of them. Every figure comes from the maker’s own product page, spec sheet or instructions, read on 18 September 2026, and where two of a maker’s documents disagree we put the less flattering figure in the table.

Three of the seven have maker documents that disagree with each other. The biggest gap is on the NRS Folding Shower Seat with Legs, Back and Arms: its product page gives a 190kg user limit, the NRS instructions give 160kg.

## The short answer

1. Aidapt Solo Deluxe Shower Seat (VB535): best overall: back, flip-up arms and a 190kg limit in every Aidapt document, folding to 190mm.
2. Aidapt Solo Standard Shower Seat (VB532): best seat-only choice: 190kg limit and the only warranty over 2 years here, 25 years on the frame.
3. NRS Folding Shower Seat with Legs (M48787): best for a tight cubicle: projects 95mm from the wall when folded, 160kg limit.
4. NRS Folding Shower Seat with Legs, Back and Arms (M53370): back and arms on an NRS frame, but the instructions say 160kg where the page says 190kg.
5. Drive DeVilbiss Wall Mounted Shower Seat with Drop Down Legs (SWALL002): widest height range here, 43 to 58cm, with a 160kg limit and a 1 year warranty.
6. Aidapt Solo Compact Padded Shower Seat with Leg (VB544): smallest wall seat: 360 x 280mm padded seat, 159kg limit.
7. Aidapt Aluminium Folding Shower Stool (VB541A): the only one that needs no drilling: freestanding, folds for travel, 120kg limit.

Review Mobility Winner 2026

Aidapt Solo Deluxe Shower Seat

Why we recommend it

The padded version of Aidapt’s Solo Deluxe: a wall-fixed seat with a backrest, arms that lift independently and legs that take some of the load. Aidapt’s page, spec sheet and fixing instructions all give 190kg, and it has the highest top seat height in this list at 615mm.

£136.63 on Amazon

Review Mobility Winner is our own editorial award. We choose it by comparing manufacturers' published specifications, prices and warranty terms. It is not a physical test, and it is not an official certification or an endorsement by any manufacturer or regulator. How we choose

## What checking the documents turned up

3 of the 7 seats have maker documents that disagree with each other. The NRS M53370 page and instructions differ on user weight (190kg against 160kg), the same NRS page gives two folded depths (166mm and 175mm), both NRS seats’ pages say 2 years’ guarantee where the instructions say 12 months, and the Drive page describes the frame as both steel and aluminium.

Only 2 of the 7 carry a 190kg user limit in every maker document we opened. Both are Aidapt Solo seats, VB535 and VB532. The NRS M53370 is listed at 190kg on its product page but 160kg in its instructions, so we list 160kg.

3 of the 7 have no warranty period in any maker document we opened. Aidapt publishes a 25 year frame warranty for the Solo Standard (VB532) but gives no period on the pages, spec sheets or instructions for the Solo Deluxe (VB535), Solo Compact (VB544) or folding stool (VB541A).

None of the 6 wall-mounted seats has a user limit that holds on any wall. All three makers leave the choice of fixings to the installer. NRS states its 160kg limit is “based on the product being fitted to a suitable surface using appropriate fixings”, and Drive says fasteners are not supplied because the fixing depends on the wall’s material and thickness.

## How we checked, and what we did not do

We did not buy, use or measure any of these products. For each one we opened the manufacturer’s UK product page and the documents it links to (leaflet, spec sheet, instructions for use), and in a few cases a copy of the maker’s instructions hosted by a dealer where the maker does not host its own. We recorded each figure with the document it came from.

Where two of the maker’s documents give different figures for the same thing, we apply the least-favourable-figure rule: the table shows the less flattering one and the text shows both. Buyers who plan around the least favourable figure are never caught out; buyers who plan around the best one sometimes are.

For wall-mounted shower seats the printed user limit is the seat’s limit, not the wall’s. We read each maker’s fixing instructions for what they say about wall type, fixings and who should fit the seat. Seat height is the maker’s quoted range from floor to seat top with the legs adjusted. Folded depth is how far the seat sticks out from the wall when folded up, which decides whether a standing user or a shower door can get past it. Where a maker gives only an unfolded depth we say the folded figure is not published. The freestanding stool has no folded-depth figure because it is not fixed to the wall.

We only included products from makers with published UK documents, and only products currently listed on Amazon UK so each pick can carry a live price box. Rankings are our judgement from the documents. No manufacturer or retailer paid to appear, and none saw this page before publication. If you think we have a figure wrong, email hello@reviewmobility.co.uk with the document and we will correct it.

## All 7 compared

Figures are the maker’s own. Where the maker’s documents disagree, the table shows the less favourable figure (see each pick for both). Amazon prices change often, so they are in the live boxes, not the table.

# Top 5 Folding Shower Seats on Amazon: Reviews and Comparisons

 By Staff Writer Last Updated April 07, 2025 

Finding the right shower seat can significantly enhance your bathing experience, especially for those with mobility challenges or anyone seeking a more comfortable way to shower. Folding shower seats are an excellent solution as they save space and offer convenience. In this article, we’ll review the top 5 folding shower seats available on Amazon, helping you make an informed choice based on quality, functionality, and customer feedback.

## Moen 8912 Home Care Folding Shower Seat

The Moen 8912 is a highly-rated folding shower seat that combines durability and style. It supports up to 400 pounds and features a sleek design that complements modern bathrooms. Made from high-quality plastic, this seat is resistant to corrosion and easy to clean. Customers love its sturdy construction and ease of installation.

## Drive Medical Folding Shower Bench

Drive Medical offers a practical option with their folding shower bench. This model is designed for individuals seeking safety without sacrificing comfort or style. With an aluminum frame that supports up to 300 pounds, it’s lightweight yet sturdy enough for everyday use. Plus, its non-slip surface provides additional safety during showers.

## AquaSense Folding Bath Seat

The AquaSense folding bath seat is another excellent selection for those looking for comfort in the shower without over-complicating their space. It has a unique design that allows it to fold flat against the wall when not in use while supporting users up to 350 pounds when deployed. Its padded seat enhances comfort during longer showers.

## Carex Health Brands Deluxe Folding Shower Seat

Carex Health Brands provide a deluxe folding shower seat designed with user-friendly features including adjustable height settings for customized comfort levels according to individual needs. The robust construction ensures stability while being compact enough not to take up much space when folded away.

## Vaunn Medical Adjustable Shower Chair with Backrest

While primarily designed as a chair rather than just a seat, the Vaunn Medical adjustable chair comes with multiple functionalities perfect for any bathroom setup needing extra support during showers—offering both backrest support and foldable capabilities which make it versatile yet straightforward. Users appreciate the ease of adjustment along with its safety features like rubber grips.

Choosing the right folding shower seat can greatly improve your bathing routine by providing necessary support while ensuring safety in slippery environments like bathrooms. Each of these top-rated options available on Amazon demonstrates unique benefits tailored toward different needs—from simple designs prioritizing practicality all the way through luxurious seating experiences—with all maintaining high standards of quality overall.

results.title: 4 Portable Shower Chair Options for Travel [pros + cons]
results.author: Alvaro Silberstein
results.text:
4 Portable Shower Chair Options for Travel [pros + cons]

 Nov 10, 2023 6 min read Accessible Travel Tips 

# 4 Portable Shower Chair Options for Travel [+ pros and cons]

Nuprodx brand travel shower chair

This article is written by Alvaro Silberstein - an avid traveler, co-founder of Wheel the World, and a C5 quadriplegic. In this article, he shares his advice and guidance on the best shower wheelchairs for travel.

Alvaro Silberstein: co-founder and CEO of Wheel the World

Shower and bathrooms are always an issue for people with a physical disability. Each of us, with different disabilities, has a different technique, equipment, and assistance needs when it comes time to take a shower. Portable shower chairs are often essential for many travelers with disabilities.

In my case, I am a complete C5 quadriplegic. I need assistance to transfer and the best solution for me is a bathroom wheelchair that lets me enter a roll-in shower to be able to shower. Some people require a bench or shower seat built within the shower and then transfer onto it. For those more daring, all they need is a plastic seat placed in the shower, or simply to transfer to a cushion on the shower or bath floor.

## Traveling with a Portable Shower Chair

Many people wonder how those who need a shower wheelchair go about traveling. Is it possible to fold it up and take it with you? 

The answer is yes, but not always.

Some shower wheelchairs have been designed specifically to be able to store easily for travel. I’ve had the opportunity to try out many different options. In this article I want to share the best alternatives for those who are looking for a travel shower wheelchair.

- Disclaimer 1: The order is random. I will go over the pros and cons of each option. As we know well, every disability is different, so we want to give as many details as possible so that you can decide based on your needs.
- Disclaimer 2: Like a lot of adaptive equipment, these chairs are expensive. Some government programs offer subsidies for them and all of these chairs last a long time. I’ve had mine for ten years.

### Can I Bring a Shower Chair on a Plane?

No, you cannot bring your shower chair on the plane. Shower chairs aren’t considered carry-ons and should be checked like other baggage. However, airlines cannot charge you to check a shower wheelchair because it’s considered essential mobility equipment. Don’t let them charge you extra!

Travel shower wheelchair by Seatara

## The Best Portable Shower Chairs to Consider for Travel

Lets get into the some options you should consider when looking for a solid shower wheelchair to bring with you during your travels.

### Go-Anywhere Portable Commode Shower Chair

Pros: The Go-Anywhere portable chair is easy to put together and take apart. You can assemble it in just five minutes or so. The first time can be a little difficult, but then it becomes like second nature after a few tries.

You can also use this shower chair in the bathtub. A slider attaches to the chair so that it can be placed in the tub without leaving the chair. It’s functional and very useful for when there is a bathtub instead of a roll-in shower.

Cons: What could be improved on this chair? Its weight, bulkiness, and carrying case. The case has wheels, but it’s very big. If you bring all of the parts including the slider, it’s a bit heavy. On long trips it can be uncomfortable to transport and it takes up a lot of space in the trunk of a car.

### Seatara Wheelable Chair

Pros: This modern and ergonomic chair was designed to accommodate smaller bathrooms and narrow doors. It has big wheels that allow users with functional movement in their arms to push themselves independently.

The best thing about this chair is its weight and how easy it is to store. It’s mostly made of plastic which makes it much lighter than its aluminum alternatives. It has an innovative design which takes less than a minute to put together and take apart. It has a compact bag that’s easy to transport and lighter than its counterparts. The carrier bag is so light, in fact, that it’s a little weak and easier to break when traveling on an airplane for example.

Cons: The con of this bathroom wheelchair is that it’s so compact that people with reduced mobility may not feel secure and stable when seated in the chair. It has a low back rest and the seat is a bit low (49 cm of space), so using a taller than normal toilet isn’t possible. It could be uncomfortable for caregivers assisting people with their bathroom procedures.

Overall, this chair is a great solution because it’s compact and easy to set up, but it’s not for everyone. It doesn’t meet certain requirements for people with less mobility (for example, tetraplegics) that need more assistance and mobility.

Seatara portable shower chair with storage bag

### Seatara BathMobile Chair

Pros: The BathMobile Chair, from the same brand as the Wheelable Chair, is the less compact and autonomous sister that is more stable and comfortable for people with less mobility. It's a foldable shower chair with a back, but still very light (more than the Goes Anywhere chair) and is as easy to transport and store.

Cons: The most complicated part of this chair is the height - with a 47cm space between the seat and the floor. It’s less than the Wheelable, which keeps it from entering some bathrooms. Accessible toilets in hotel rooms are often higher than normal (designed with the elderly in mind). This can be an issue for those who use this chair. 

Although this chair has small wheels and was designed to be used with assistance, a user with more mobility can change them to larger wheels to be able to push it. But, these wheels will not fit in the carrying case.

### Nuprodx Model MC4000TX Chair

Pros: This model of shower wheelchair is compact when it’s stored away and has a relatively small carrying case. It’s stable and made to be assisted like the Goes Anywhere and BathMobile chairs. You can adjust the height of the chair and, therefore, the space between the seat and the floor from its legs. It takes about 5 minutes to set up and one person can do it easily. It’s easier to set up than the Wheelable and the BathMobile and a little simpler than the Goes Anywhere.

Cons: It’s case is easy to transport and tough, although it’s a little heavy compared to the Seatara chairs.

In my opinion, this the best solution for those with less stability like me because it has other optional features like a headrest and seat belt.

## Final Thoughts

These are four options of shower wheelchairs that can be folded up and stored in a transportable case to bring with you on a trip. It’s important to mention that there are many people with a physical disability who can make it work without needing one of these chairs while traveling. If that’s you, traveling is even easier.

If you know of any other shower wheelchairs that are good options, don’t hesitate to reach out to us so that we can improve this article and add more options. Comment your suggestions below!

Wheel the World is a community that invites everyone to participate and share experiences for a more accessible world.

# The best shower chairs, as recommended by experts

From the best shower chair for independent seniors to shower chairs for those who need extra support, check out our expert-backed round-up.

 by Tonya Russell Updated on: May 12, 2026 5 min read 

 

## In this article

- Best shower chairs for independent seniors 
- Best shower chairs for seniors who need extra support 
- Consider a handheld shower head
- The bottom line on shower chairs

When an older loved one starts to show signs of impaired mobility, it may be time to consider the accessibility of their home. One of the spaces in which they’re the most vulnerable: the bathroom. To protect your loved one, you might want to invest in a shower chair, which can minimize the risk of injury on a slippery surface — something that’s incredibly important, since more than one in four Americans over age 65 suffer a fall each year, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).

An older adult may need a product that can help them get in and out of the shower, maintain their balance or simply provide a place to rest, notes Susan Adamowicz, OTR, an occupational therapist at McLean Health Center in Simsbury, Connecticut. “Having a seat provides them the support that can allow them to continue participating in bathing while sitting,” she says.

Whether you’re just starting to research or you’re ready to buy, here are the best shower chairs on the market.

## Best shower chairs for independent seniors 

### 1. Clevr Teak Wood Folding Shower Seat

Image via Wayfair

Some people need a seat daily, while others may feel comfortable knowing that they have one for when they aren’t feeling their best. Even some tasks, like feet washing, may require a minute of sitting. This teak seat is one of the best looking. It folds away, and when it’s down, seniors may be able to rely on the tiles if necessary. This can also be paired with a bar for extra safety. 

Where to buy: Teak Wood Folding Shower Seat ($166, Wayfair)

### 2. Carex Bath Seat and Shower Chair

Image via Amazon

Reviewers of this chair say that it is sturdy and built to last. The $44 chair is a good fit for a senior who may be at risk of falling in the shower but still wants to remain independent. Hafiz finds this chair to be a good option for those who need the minimum amount of support. 

Where to buy: Carex Bath Seat and Shower Chair ($50, Amazon)

### 3. OasisSpace Heavy Duty Shower Chair

Image via Walmart

When other chairs don’t fit, this $60 space-saving shower chair can do the trick. It would be better suited for a smaller person because of how narrow it is or a senior who wants the reinforcement of a chair if they are feeling too weak to shower some days. It also comes with a bonus grab bar for the shower wall. 

Where to buy: Kekoy Heavy Duty Shower Chair ($48, Walmart)

### 4. NOVA Shower and Bath Chair

Image via Amazon

The NOVA chair is probably one of the most basic and what is most familiar to someone looking for a chair. At 8.4 pounds, it is also one of the lightest chairs one could own, so it would be easy for a more independent senior to set the chair up themselves.

## Best shower chairs for seniors who need extra support 

### 5. Drive Medical RTL Handicap Bathroom Bench

Image via Amazon

According to Hafiz, “A bench is best for someone who can’t step over a tub. It allows them to sit on the chair and then swing their legs over.” 

This bench sits outside of your tub and makes it easy to get in if you have an injury or are ever unsteady stepping over the edge. One owner warns that her floor got wet, but that can easily be remedied with a bath mat to prevent slipping when you’re out of the shower. 

### 6. Carousel Sliding Transfer Bench with Swivel Seat

Image via Amazon

This chair is professional grade — similar to what you’d see in a medical setting. While it isn’t necessary to spend over $100 for a chair, this may still be a preferred choice for someone who is paralyzed or who has limited vision or control over their movement. It features a padded seat and a belt to keep someone in place, and the swivel is helpful for placing a person into it. 

### 7. DMI Tub Transfer Bench

Image via Amazon

This bench and shower chair requires no tools for assembly and can be adjusted high enough for an easy transfer from a wheelchair to the bathtub. It has a safety strap and a sliding seat, which is ideal for someone who needs assistance in the shower. 

## Consider a handheld shower head

Whether you choose a shower chair, bench, or stool, a handheld shower head is a relatively inexpensive investment (most cost around $50) that can make a big difference for people with impaired mobility. “They can bring the water to them rather than just sitting and having it bombard them from a stationary shower head,” says Scott Trudeau, PhD, OTR, a productive aging practice manager with the American Occupational Therapy Association. 

## The bottom line on shower chairs

If you’re not sure which type of shower chair will work best, see if a local senior center or agency has an equipment loan program that will let you test a certain style in the space before committing, advises Trudeau. There are also many options available online, and websites usually provide the specific dimensions so you can measure it for your shower or tub.

Additional reporting by Michelle Felton
